principles.name: segmentation
principles.heuristic: Split the conflicting system, responsibility, data, or workflow into independently changeable parts so each can be optimized without forcing the same trade-off on the whole.

principles.name: extraction
principles.heuristic: Extract or isolate the component, responsibility, data, behavior, or dependency causing the harmful effect, or retain only the part actually required.

principles.name: local quality
principles.heuristic: Replace uniform treatment with locally specialized structure, behavior, configuration, or policy so each part operates under conditions suited to its role.

principles.name: asymmetry
principles.heuristic: Break unnecessary symmetry: allow different components, replicas, paths, users, or states to have different roles or policies when identical treatment creates the conflict.

principles.name: consolidation
principles.heuristic: Combine compatible components, resources, requests, or operations in space or time when duplication, separation, or coordination overhead creates the conflict.

principles.name: universality
principles.heuristic: Let one component or abstraction perform several compatible functions so redundant components, interfaces, dependencies, or transformations can be removed.

principles.name: nesting
principles.heuristic: Compose components, scopes, containers, or abstractions hierarchically so one can contain, encapsulate, or pass through another.

principles.name: counterweight
principles.heuristic: Offset load, latency, cost, risk, or resource pressure with a compensating mechanism rather than strengthening the constrained mechanism directly.

principles.name: prior counteraction
principles.heuristic: Apply a compensating or protective action before an expected harmful effect occurs so the later effect is neutralized when it arrives.

principles.name: preliminary action
principles.heuristic: Precompute, preload, prefetch, preconfigure, validate, reserve, or position what will be needed before the latency-sensitive or failure-sensitive path begins.

principles.name: cushion in advance
principles.heuristic: Prepare redundancy, rollback, fallback, reserve capacity, circuit breaking, recovery data, or other emergency protection before a failure occurs.

principles.name: equipotentiality
principles.heuristic: Equalize states, representations, interfaces, privileges, or operating levels so useful work no longer requires repeated expensive transitions between them.

principles.name: do it in reverse
principles.heuristic: Reverse direction, responsibility, dependency, ownership, control flow, or operation; make the active side passive or the fixed side movable when the conventional direction creates the conflict.

principles.name: spheroidality
principles.heuristic: Replace unnecessarily linear structures or flows with cyclic, ring, rotational, curved, or recursive organization when linearity creates the constraint.

principles.name: dynamicity
principles.heuristic: Make components, parameters, policies, capacity, topology, or bindings adjustable and reconfigurable so behavior can change with operating conditions.

principles.name: partial or excessive action
principles.heuristic: When the exact target is expensive or difficult to achieve directly, deliberately under-shoot or over-shoot it and handle the smaller remaining difference separately.

principles.name: transition into a new dimension
principles.heuristic: Add an axis, layer, hierarchy, partition, channel, dimension, or level of indirection to escape a constraint imposed by the current representation.

principles.name: mechanical vibration
principles.heuristic: Replace static behavior with controlled oscillation, pulsing, polling, heartbeats, resonance, or higher-frequency interaction when periodic variation exposes a better operating regime.

principles.name: periodic action
principles.heuristic: Replace continuous work with periodic, event-driven, scheduled, sampled, or batched action; tune the cadence and use the gaps for other useful work.

principles.name: continuity of useful action
principles.heuristic: Keep useful work flowing and minimize idle or intermediate stages through streaming, pipelining, concurrency, background processing, or reuse of otherwise idle capacity.

principles.name: rushing through
principles.heuristic: Perform an unavoidable harmful, inconsistent, blocked, or risky transitional state quickly so the system spends the minimum possible time exposed to it.

principles.name: convert harm into benefit
principles.heuristic: Turn a harmful factor, waste product, failure mode, contention signal, or rejected result into a useful resource or signal; combine harmful effects when doing so can neutralize them.

principles.name: feedback
principles.heuristic: Observe the actual outcome and feed it back into control decisions so behavior adapts instead of accepting the trade-off; change the feedback loop when the existing one is ineffective or unstable.

principles.name: intermediary
principles.heuristic: Insert a mediator, proxy, adapter, broker, queue, cache, buffer, gateway, or temporary abstraction between conflicting parties.

principles.name: self-service
principles.heuristic: Make a component observe, maintain, heal, configure, replenish, or clean up itself, and reuse otherwise wasted outputs or resources where practical.

principles.name: copying
principles.heuristic: Operate on a replica, cache, snapshot, proxy, model, simulation, projection, or transformed representation when operating on the original is expensive, dangerous, unavailable, or disruptive.

principles.name: dispose
principles.heuristic: Replace an expensive long-lived element with inexpensive disposable or ephemeral instances when durability, lifecycle, or cleanup guarantees create unnecessary complexity.

principles.name: replacement of mechanical system
principles.heuristic: Replace direct or tightly coupled interaction with signals, metadata, events, sensing, declarative rules, virtualization, or another more controllable interaction mechanism.

principles.name: pneumatic or hydraulic constructions
principles.heuristic: Replace rigidly provisioned capacity with elastic or flow-based mechanisms such as queues, streams, pools, buffers, backpressure, or dynamically allocated resources.

principles.name: flexible membranes or thin films
principles.heuristic: Use a lightweight flexible boundary such as a wrapper, facade, policy layer, filter, interceptor, or virtual boundary instead of rigid structural separation.

principles.name: porous material
principles.heuristic: Make a boundary selectively permeable using controlled openings, filters, extension points, plugins, admission rules, sampling, or pre-established channels.

principles.name: changing the color
principles.heuristic: Change representation, labeling, visibility, transparency, telemetry, or observability so otherwise hidden state, differences, or behavior become distinguishable.

principles.name: homogeneity
principles.heuristic: Make interacting elements use the same or closely compatible representation, protocol, abstraction, runtime, or substrate to reduce conversion and mismatch costs.

principles.name: rejecting and regenerating parts
principles.heuristic: Expire, discard, release, recycle, or transform elements after their useful function is complete, and regenerate or restore them when they become necessary again.

principles.name: transformation of properties
principles.heuristic: Resolve the conflict by changing state, configuration, granularity, consistency, concentration, flexibility, precision, capacity, or another governing parameter rather than redesigning the whole system.

principles.name: phase transition
principles.heuristic: Move the element into a qualitatively different operating state, mode, representation, or lifecycle phase whose properties remove the original conflict.

principles.name: thermal expansion
principles.heuristic: Use controlled expansion or contraction of capacity, scope, buffering, replication, or resource allocation in response to changing operating conditions.

principles.name: accelerated oxidation
principles.heuristic: Increase the strength or activation level of an enabling mechanism stepwise—such as validation, enforcement, isolation, replication, or signal intensity—when a weaker interaction requires compensating complexity.

principles.name: inert environment
principles.heuristic: Run the interaction in an isolated, neutralized, sandboxed, side-effect-free, simulated, or otherwise controlled environment so harmful interactions cannot propagate.

principles.name: composite materials
principles.heuristic: Combine heterogeneous components, representations, storage models, algorithms, or execution strategies so the composite provides properties that a uniform design cannot.
